findings.finding: The plan states 'Jira 8.17.1 defaults to 50' as the effective server page size for `jira.search.views.default.max`, but this is factually incorrect per Atlassian's own documentation. The 50-issue figure is the response size when maxResults is omitted entirely from the request. When maxResults is passed (as both `_paged_search` and `_iter_pages` do — passing 100), the server honors the request up to `jira.search.views.default.max`, whose documented default is 1000. An implementer reading the plan's claim may seed only 2*50+1=101 issues expecting to exercise three pages of 50, when the actual pager (_paged_search uses page_size=100, _iter_pages uses page_size=100) would fetch all 101 in a single page — exercising zero pagination. The 'observe first' instruction partially mitigates this, but a wrong expectation anchors the implementer's interpretation of what the observation means.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria — pagination bullet: 'Jira 8.17.1 defaults to 50, but `jira.search.views.default.max` is server-configurable and the server silently truncates'
scenarios: Implementer seeds 101 issues (2*50+1) expecting three 50-issue pages, but _paged_search fetches them in a single page of 100 + one empty terminal page — pagination is not exercised and the criterion is satisfied by a one-page fetch.

findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'Jira 8.17.1 defaults to 50' with: 'the pager requests page_size=100; the server cap `jira.search.views.default.max` defaults to 1000 but may be lower on this harness — the observation step will tell you the effective cap'. The plan acknowledges `JIRA_DC_BASE_URL` as the env var but does not direct the write step or the assertion to read from it — leaving both steps free to hardcode the default literal.
findings.finding: The config-file AC hardcodes the harness URL string `http://localhost:2990/jira` in two places: the rebar.toml write step and the 'assert the SET of distinct values is exactly {the harness URL}' assertion. If the test implementation repeats the string literal rather than deriving it from `JIRA_DC_BASE_URL`, a port or host change (e.g., for parallel CI, a different compose profile, or a harness upgrade) breaks both the write and the assertion without a clear error — the assertion will fire on the new URL but the error message will show a hardcoded expected value that no longer matches reality.

evidence: 'rows 2-13 (and outbound row 14) share ONE fixture, `bound_dc_issue(...)`, which: (1) creates a DC issue via dc_transport.create_issue; (2) runs a WRITING-MODE inbound pass so the local ticket and its binding exist; (3) returns (local_id, dc_key). The fixture must ASSERT the binding exists before yielding'
'SCOPE EVERY MUTATION PASS WITH --filter-local-ids... OR IT WILL TRY TO CREATE THE WHOLE STORE COPY IN DC'

The README.md scope line says 'document the isolation contract and WHY (auto-push)' — no mention of the bound_dc_issue protocol or the filter-local-ids requirement, which are equally load-bearing for any future contributor.
findings.finding: The `bound_dc_issue` fixture is the shared prerequisite for all 28 outbound mutation cells (rows 2–14) and carries a precise four-step protocol whose violation silently degrades every dependent cell from UPDATE to CREATE (producing a green-but-wrong result the plan explicitly names as a failure mode). The plan directs the fixture to be implemented but does not direct its protocol to be captured anywhere durable — not in the README, not as a module-level docstring, not in AGENTS.md. A contributor adding a new outbound mutation cell who is unaware of the protocol will fall into exactly the CREATE-instead-of-UPDATE trap without any compile-time or lint-time warning.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria — 'REQUIRED SEQUENCING FOR OUTBOUND ROWS 2-13' section; Scope — 'tests/external/live_jira_dc/' and 'README.md'
scenarios: A contributor adds a 15th outbound mutation cell, uses a plain local-ticket fixture instead of `bound_dc_issue`, and gets a green test that is actually asserting a freshly-created issue rather than an updated one — the CREATE-instead-of-UPDATE trap the plan names.
A contributor omits `--filter-local-ids` from a new mutation cell's pass invocation, causing the pass to attempt creating all ~10^3 store-copy tickets in the harness, timing out the job.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the README.md scope (or as a doc comment at the top of the dc_mutations helper) a 'Adding a new mutation cell' section that states: (1) all outbound UPDATE cells must use the `bound_dc_issue` fixture; (2) every mutation pass must include `--filter-local-ids <local_id>`; (3) the reason for (1) is that the scrub removes all bindings, so an unscoped pass routes every ticket to CREATE; (4) the fixture asserts the binding exists before yielding and will fail loudly if the inbound pass did not establish it.

findings.finding: The outbound oracle for mutation Row 1 (create) mandates reading `GET /rest/api/2/issue/{key}/properties/local_id` via raw REST, and the plan correctly notes that `JiraDataCenterTransport` has no getter. This endpoint surface has never been exercised live against the DC 8.17.1 harness: no live test in `tests/external/live_jira_dc/` calls it, and the existing `set_entity_property` live coverage is WRITE-only (unit tests fake the client; no live test calls `_client.add_issue_property` and then reads back via the REST properties endpoint). The response shape is unverified — Jira's issue-properties GET endpoint returns `{"key": "local_id", "value": <stored_value>}`, so the test must read `.value` from the response body, not the top-level body; but if DC 8.17.1 returns a different shape (or 404s the endpoint for a property set via `add_issue_property`), the oracle is silently wrong. Without a live probe of this specific GET surface, the plan is asserting a capability that is Unverified against the target instance.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria — Row 1 outbound oracle: 'entity property `local_id` read by RAW REST — `GET /rest/api/2/issue/{key}/properties/local_id`'

If the response body shape is {"key": "local_id", "value": "abc..."}, the test must read body['value'], not body itself — a shape assumption that silently fails if the property was never written or the key is wrong

Neither case satisfies the plan's stated purpose ('prove the specific failure that made the previous run meaningless' — the prior `scanned=0` was partly because the local store was empty, and `scanned` does not measure local store size).
